display.name: EMQX
display.description: EMQX MQTT broker health from metrics the broker exports natively over OTLP: connections, throughput, message loss, subscriptions, authentication, and Erlang VM runtime.

display.name: service.name
display.description: EMQX service name. Defaults to emqx unless the broker sets OTEL_SERVICE_NAME.

display.name: service.instance.id
display.description: EMQX node name, for example emqx@10.0.1.7.

display.name: Cluster Size
display.description: Number of nodes in the EMQX cluster, as reported by each node. A standalone broker reports 1.

display.name: Nodes Stopped
display.description: Cluster members currently down (node.stopped). Anything above zero means the cluster is degraded.

display.name: Connections
display.description: Current MQTT connections across the selected nodes (connections.count). Includes persistent sessions whose client is offline.

display.name: Sessions
display.description: Current MQTT sessions across the selected nodes (sessions.count).

display.name: Connections by Node
display.description: connections.count against live_connections.count per node. A widening gap means persistent sessions are accumulating without their clients being attached.

display.name: Sessions and Channels by Node
display.description: sessions.count, cluster_sessions.count and channels.count per node. Channels track the connection processes each node is running.

display.name: Connection Churn
display.description: Rate of client.connected and client.disconnected. Sustained symmetric churn usually means clients are reconnect-looping rather than holding sessions.

display.name: Session Lifecycle
display.description: Sessions created, resumed, taken over, discarded and terminated per interval. Takeovers spike when two clients share a client ID.

display.name: Connections: Current vs Peak
display.description: Current counts against the peak EMQX has recorded since the node started (connections.max, live_connections.max, sessions.max). Useful for sizing.

display.name: Message Rate In / Out
display.description: messages.received against messages.sent, per second.

display.name: Delivery and Acknowledgement Rate
display.description: messages.delivered against messages.acked. A persistent gap means QoS 1/2 subscribers are not acknowledging what the broker hands them.

display.name: Bytes In / Out
display.description: bytes.received against bytes.sent, per second. The counters are byte counts despite the kb unit label EMQX puts on the OTLP export.

display.name: MQTT Packets In / Out
display.description: packets.received against packets.sent, per second. Counts every MQTT control packet, not just PUBLISH.

display.name: Received Messages by QoS
display.description: Publish rate split by the QoS the client used.

display.name: Sent Messages by QoS
display.description: Outbound rate split by the QoS the broker delivered at.

display.name: Publish, Forward and Store
display.description: messages.publish, messages.forward (routed to another cluster node), messages.retained, messages.persisted and messages.delayed.

display.name: Rule Engine
display.description: rules.matched, actions.executed and actions.messages. Zero on a broker with no rules configured.

display.name: Messages Dropped
display.description: messages.dropped over the selected range: publishes the broker never routed.

display.name: Deliveries Dropped
display.description: delivery.dropped over the selected range: messages the broker routed but never handed to the subscriber.

display.name: PUBLISH Errors
display.description: packets.publish.error over the selected range: PUBLISH packets EMQX rejected.

display.name: CONNACK Errors
display.description: packets.connack.error over the selected range: connection attempts refused.

display.name: Messages Dropped by Node
display.description: messages.dropped per interval, per node.

display.name: Message Drops by Reason
display.description: Why publishes were dropped: no matching subscriber, expired, rate quota exceeded, or the receiver's receive-maximum window was full.

display.name: Deliveries Dropped by Node
display.description: delivery.dropped per interval, per node.

display.name: Delivery Drops by Reason
display.description: Why deliveries were dropped. queue_full is the one to alert on: the subscriber's message queue overflowed and data was discarded.

display.name: Packet Errors
display.description: PUBLISH and CONNACK packets EMQX rejected, including authorization failures, duplicate packet IDs (inuse) and rate-limit rejections.

display.name: Missed QoS Acknowledgements
display.description: PUBACK / PUBREC / PUBREL / PUBCOMP packets that arrived with no in-flight message waiting for them. A rising count points at clients replaying or duplicating acks.

display.name: Topics
display.description: Current topic count (topics.count). EMQX replicates this value to every node, so the dashboard takes the maximum across nodes rather than the sum. With more than one cluster selected, it shows the largest cluster rather than a combined total; select a single service.name for a total.

display.name: Subscriptions
display.description: Current subscription count (subscriptions.count).

display.name: Routes
display.description: Current routing table entries (routes.count). Grows with distinct subscribed topic filters across the cluster. EMQX replicates this value to every node, so the dashboard takes the maximum across nodes rather than the sum. With more than one cluster selected, it shows the largest cluster rather than a combined total; select a single service.name for a total.

display.name: Retained Messages
display.description: Current retained messages held by the broker (retained.count). EMQX replicates this value to every node, so the dashboard takes the maximum across nodes rather than the sum. With more than one cluster selected, it shows the largest cluster rather than a combined total; select a single service.name for a total.

display.name: Subscriptions and Subscribers
display.description: subscriptions.count, subscriptions.shared.count, durable_subscriptions.count and subscribers.count over time. Shared and durable subscription counts are cluster-wide, so they use the maximum across nodes; subscriptions and subscribers are node-local sums.

display.name: Topics, Routes and Retained
display.description: topics.count, routes.count and retained.count over time. Retained messages stay in the broker until a client overwrites them with an empty payload, so this line only comes down deliberately. EMQX replicates this value to every node, so the dashboard takes the maximum across nodes rather than the sum.

display.name: Subscribe / Unsubscribe Rate
display.description: client.subscribe and client.unsubscribe per interval.

display.name: Subscribe Packets and Errors
display.description: SUBSCRIBE / UNSUBSCRIBE packets against the SUBACK / UNSUBACK the broker returned, plus rejected subscribe attempts.

display.name: Authentication Outcomes
display.description: authentication.success against authentication.failure, with the anonymous share broken out. A failure spike with steady connect attempts means credentials broke.

display.name: Authorization Outcomes
display.description: authorization.allow, deny, nomatch and superuser per interval. nomatch means no ACL rule applied and the default policy decided.

display.name: Authorization Cache
display.description: authorization.cache_hit against cache_miss. A low hit ratio pushes every publish and subscribe through the ACL backend.

display.name: Banned and Flapping Clients
display.description: client.banned plus flapping detections by client ID, peer host and username. Flapping means a client crossed the reconnect threshold and was quarantined.

display.name: CONNACK Outcomes
display.description: CONNACK packets sent against the error and auth-error subsets, alongside client.authenticate and client.authorize hook invocations.

display.name: CPU Use by Node
display.description: cpu.use per node, as a percentage of the node's CPU.

display.name: Erlang Run Queue by Node
display.description: run.queue per node: processes ready to run but waiting for a scheduler. A run queue that stays above the scheduler count means the VM is CPU bound.

display.name: Memory Used vs Total by Node
display.description: used.memory against total.memory per node, in bytes.

display.name: Memory Utilization by Node
display.description: used.memory as a percentage of total.memory, per node.

display.name: Process Mailbox Sizes by Node
display.description: broker.pool.max.mailbox.size and mnesia.tm.mailbox.size. A growing mailbox means a core process is falling behind the message flow.
